MIND THE GAP:
FINDING A BETTER WAY TO PRESENT GAPS & GAP TRENDS

 Damian W Betebenner
 National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
 Dover, New Hampshire October 3rd, 2017

ACHIEVEMENT GAPS

• IMHO, the most abused and misunderstood of academic
 indicators.

• With the advent of criterion-referenced testing, gaps in
 percent pro cient have become ubiquitous.

• Used as part of almost all state accountability systems.

• Not only gaps themselves but trends in gap statistics.

SCRATCH A CRITERION AND YOU FIND A
NORM

• It’s not clear (to me) that scale score based gap/gap-trend indicators are (much
 of) an improvement.

• One loses the important pro ciency cut as a reference point in the gap.

• Even with pro ciency based cuts, it’s not clear that they are that interpretable.

 • Is a 20% gap between economically and non-economically disadvantaged
 students the same: 0%/20%, 40%/60%, and 80%/100%.

• This takes me back to the same deliberations I went through when thinking
 about student growth and writing Norm- and criterion-referenced student growth.

NORM- AND CRITERION-REFERENCED GAP METRICS
• Goal: Produce a metric-free distributional comparison for looking at gaps.

• Goal: Communicate a 50th percentile student who is white lies at what
 percentile of the overall distribution.

• Extend: Communicate an Xth percentile student who is of ethnicity Y lies at
 what percentile of the overall distribution.

• Extend: Do this for other groups (e.g., (non)-economically disadvantaged)

• Question: Would it be better to depict where an overall Xth percentile student
 like in each of the ethnicity speci c distributions? Problem (bigger numbers are
 worse).

• Gaps a achievement level cuts can be depicted by locating cut graphically.

CONCLUSIONS & NEXT STEPS

• Gap and gap trends summarizations at a single point of the distribution
 necessarily lead to information loss.

• Lots of simulation work to be done regarding comparisons of different a gap
 metrics.

• Possibly apply to NAEP data.

• Not sure whether applicable for accountability purposes.
